newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Pou Chen up on ex-bonus issue.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Pou Chen up on ex-bonus issue.

text.p: Shares of Taiwan's leading shoemaker Pou Chen Industrial surged at mid-morning on Friday on its ex-bonus issue date, and brokers said they expected more rises ahead.

Pou Chen on Friday issued a stock dividend, or bonus issue, of T$3.5 per share, paying 350 shares free for every 1,000 shares held, brokers said. After 80 minutes, at 0220 GMT, Pou Chen rose the daily seven percent limit to T$117, while the overall index gained 0.88 percent.
"Pou Chen is one of the stars among so called China-concept shares, and I believe it has room to rise further," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.

China-concept shares -- Taiwan firms with active or planned investments in the communist mainland -- had surged last week -- reflecting big gains by Hong Kong's China-linked shares ahead of the British colony's July 1 handover to Beijing.
Yang said he forecast Pou Chen would enjoy a 1997 earnings per share of T$5.2 after the bonus issue.
Pou Chen, whose owners reportedly have indirect interests in a Shanghai bank, designs and makes high-end shoes in Taiwan and produces low-end shoes in China and Vietnam, Yang said.
